bills.title: Protecting kids from deepfakes and exploitative images.
Ban on government social scoring with AI.
Biometric data and license plate readers-regulation.

reading.body:
Wyoming's 2026 AI-related legislative activity spans three bills, all focused on civil liberties and child protection rather than on infrastructure, procurement, or economic development.

The three measures address distinct but related concerns: shielding minors from AI-generated exploitative imagery, prohibiting government use of AI for social scoring, and regulating biometric data collection alongside license plate readers. The pattern is protective rather than permissive, oriented toward constraining specific harms rather than enabling AI deployment or investment.

The data covers only enacted or tracked legislation as of March 2026 and does not indicate whether any of these bills passed, failed, or remain pending. Nothing in the dataset speaks to Wyoming's power grid, data center construction, or compute capacity, so no connection to AI scaling infrastructure can be drawn from it.
